Scaling

Language-model scaling becomes measurable

Empirical relationships connected language-model loss with parameters, data, and compute.

Jared Kaplan and colleagues

The contribution

The authors measured how language-model performance varied with model size, dataset size, and training compute. Approximate scaling relationships offered a way to reason about resource allocation within the studied training regimes.

What this does not establish

These are empirical relationships over investigated ranges. They do not prove indefinite improvement, factual reliability, or inevitable general intelligence.

Why this date?

The first arXiv submission was 23 January 2020.

This entry follows the linked publication. Read the source and date conventions.
